newsitem.title: INDIA: INSTANT ANALYSIS-Indian bankers praise RBI policy.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT ANALYSIS-Indian bankers praise RBI policy.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) unveiled its monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March) on Saturday. Following are some of the reactions from bankers and analysts.
** S.H.Khan, chairman and managing director, Industrial Development Bank of India.

"The policy is on expected lines. It has made an attempt to increase the availability of funds and to lower the cost of funds for borrowers. The increase in the availability of funds is timely. The RBI has given clear indications that there should be fall in interest rates. This should be a major boost to industry. With an increase in export credit targets, exporters will also be benefited. All in all, a good policy."
** K.Kannan, chairman and managing director, Bank of Baroda

"This is a good policy. It meets the expectations of a wide cross-section.... industry, exporters, stock market. A good deal of operational freedom is also being given to banks to determine their own interest rates and spreads over prime rates. The decision to allow banks to frame their own guidelines for consortium lending are welcome. Each bank can now strike out on its own. But it remains to be seen how the banks use their freedom."
** Kiran Nanda, economist, Gujarat Ambuja Cement

"The RBI has taken into account the apprehensions of industry about availabilty and cost of funds. There are clear signals that the RBI wants interest rates to come down. It has also indicated its commitment to exports. However fiscal issues which impact on interest rates have not even been mentioned in the policy. Government borrowings are a major factor in determining interest rates and it is not clear what is being done about this."

"I think overall the policy is positive and should improve market sentiments. It is an attempt to kickstart the economy. The steps announced in the policy should help banks improve their profitability. Liquidity should improve substantially with the cuts in CRR. Further, the move to allow FCNR (B) funds to be deployed locally will ensure that a lot of funds which are idly parked abroad will be put to productive use in India. This should help improve liquidity as well as production."
** Hemendra Kothari, chairman, DSP Financial Consultants.
"The CRR cut will definitely inject liquidity into the market but more importantly for stock markets, allowing banks to invest in secondary market will psychologically give a good boost."
** Sachin Joneja, research head, Classic Share and Stock Broking

"Basically, the policy recognises market perceptions on liquidity and interest rates. The policy is a boost to the market psychologically as well as in terms of investible funds though the latter could be less than the former. Allowing banks into the secondary market is a further step in the integration of the financial markets, permitting free flow of money between financial markets to correct imbalances in any of them. I think the current oversold market should now see a correction."
